explain.say: Morning and evening, maids heard the goblins cry: come buy, come buy. Christina Rossetti published Goblin Market in 1862, a strange, musical poem about two sisters, Laura and Lizzie, and the goblin men who sell magic fruit by a stream. The panels follow Laura's fall and rescue.

explain.say: Look at the second panel. Laura has no money, so she pays with a curl of her golden hair and gorges on the fruit. Next day she can no longer hear the goblins, and she wastes away like her friend Jeanie, who died after eating it. What makes a pleasure dangerous when you can never have it again?

explain.say: Now Lizzie, in panels four and five. She takes a silver penny to buy fruit for her sister, but refuses to eat. The goblins pinch her and smear her with juice. She runs home and tells Laura to taste it from her face. Laura's fever breaks and she is healed. Who is the real hero here?

explain.say: Critics read the poem many ways. Sort the clues on the board. A Christian reading sees temptation, a fall and a saving sacrifice. A feminist reading sees sisters who rescue each other without any man. An economic reading notices the title: a market, where a woman's body becomes payment. Which reading feels strongest?

explain.say: The poem ends years later, with both sisters, now mothers, telling their children there is no friend like a sister. Around this time Rossetti volunteered at a refuge in Highgate for women society called fallen. Wonderful. Challenge: read it aloud and notice how the uneven rhymes speed up like a market crowd.

faq.a: Two sisters, Laura and Lizzie, hear goblin men selling fruit. Laura eats and wastes away; Lizzie braves the goblins without eating and brings back the juice that saves her. It is a fairy tale about temptation, sacrifice and sisterly love.

faq.q: Is Goblin Market a children's poem?
faq.a: It looks like a fairy tale and has been printed for children, but its sensual imagery and adult themes mean it is mostly read as a poem for adults.

faq.q: What do the goblin fruits symbolise?
faq.a: Readings differ: forbidden pleasure or sin, as in Eden; sexual temptation; or consumer goods and the market. The poem keeps all of these in play.

faq.q: Why does Lizzie not eat the fruit?
faq.a: She knows eating it destroyed Jeanie and is destroying Laura. By refusing to eat while the goblins attack her, she brings the juice home on her skin, and it becomes the cure.

faq.q: Is Goblin Market about fallen women?
faq.a: Some critics link it to Rossetti's volunteer work at a Highgate home for women who had been sex workers or had children outside marriage. The poem lets a fallen sister be saved and loved, not punished.

facts: Goblin Market appeared in 1862 in Goblin Market and Other Poems, with illustrations by Christina's brother Dante Gabriel Rossetti.
Her brother Dante Gabriel co-founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood in 1848.
